The thinking behind the build

Let’s work out what
your site needs to do.

You know your business. I’ll help turn that knowledge into pages people can understand and use.

01

Put the useful information first.

Your services, the work you’ve done, and the questions customers ask before hiring you. We’ll give each a place, then shape the design around it.

02

Make the next step obvious.

A call, a quote request, a booking, or a purchase. We’ll choose the right route and ask for the information you actually need to handle it.

03

Think beyond the submit button.

If inquiries need to reach a spreadsheet, calendar, or customer system, I can plan that connection with the website.

See a working example

You’ll review the design with me before launch. Pages, features, content, revisions, price, and timing are agreed before the build starts.

Before you commit

The practical details.

Cost, control, and what happens after the site goes live.

What will it cost?

I quote for the pages, content, and features we agree on. Hosting, domain renewals, and any paid tools are identified separately, so you can see both the build cost and the costs of keeping it running.

Can I make my own updates?

Yes, if that’s how you want to manage it. We’ll choose a suitable editing setup and go through it together. You can also send changes to me, arrange ongoing support, or use a mix of both.

Who controls the website and accounts?

Your domain and business accounts should be registered to you. The handover covers the agreed site files, account access, and connection notes. Any platform, licensing, or transfer limits are discussed before the build.

What happens after launch?

Support is agreed for your project: individual updates, ongoing care, or a combination. We’ll set out the work covered, how to request it, and what it costs.
